description_full: Reformation Inc. manufactures and sells sustainable women's clothing and accessories in the United States and Internationally. It offers dresses, tops, pants, skirts, shorts, jeans, sweaters, shoes, jumpsuits, two-piece sets, outerwear, sleep and loungewear, swimwear, and accessories. The company also offers wedding collection. It retails its product through website, online channels, and stores, well as through wholesalers and other channels. The company was formerly known as REF Topco, Inc. and changed its name to Reformation Inc. in April 2025. Reformation Inc. was founded in 2009 and is headquartered in Vernon, California.
ceo_bio: Ms. Hali  Borenstein | CEO, President & Director | Age 40 | Compensation: $1.7M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1K people. Revenue per employee of $367K ranks in the below the sector median among Consumer Cyclical peers. Stock-based compensation of $793 per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 5× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: Reformation Inc. is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $1.1B market cap on $507M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +19% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 64% confirm genuine pricing power.
The company is burning through $18M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 6.5× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 62% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
